Explanation: A completed ride is the core value unit: a rider is matched with a driver, transported from pickup to destination and the trip is completed through the Uber platform.
Uber owns and operates the technology platform that matches riders with drivers, coordinates pricing and payments, and sets the rules for participating in the marketplace.
Uber has to keep enough riders and drivers active in each local market so that riders can get a car quickly and drivers can find paid trips without too much idle time.
Uber earns more when more trips are completed and when the marketplace is liquid enough that riders and drivers keep returning.
Demand and driver supply can change by neighborhood and time of day. Uber also has to operate under different transport, labor, safety and pricing rules across many countries and cities.
Uber coordinates the trip and earns Mobility revenue mainly from service fees paid by drivers for use of the platform, as well as other rider charges in some markets.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Request / Pay — The rider tells Uber where they want to go and pays for the completed trip through the platform or another supported method. | → Provider · Trip Offer — Uber's matching system sends a ride request to an available driver based on location and other marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Match / ETA — Uber shows the rider the matched driver, vehicle and estimated arrival information and coordinates the trip in the app. | → Provider · Payout — Uber coordinates driver earnings and settlement after the trip, subject to the local pricing and fee structure.

Explanation: Uber sets platform rules for driver eligibility, vehicle requirements, conduct, safety, ratings, payments and how trips are offered and priced, subject to local law.
The rider and driver apps are the main access points, supported by Uber's global brand, referrals, promotions and local marketing.
Uber runs the apps, predicts demand, matches riders and drivers, calculates prices and ETAs, processes payments, supports users and manages safety and marketplace quality.
Important resources include the installed rider and driver base, trip and location data, matching and pricing systems, routing technology, payments infrastructure and the Uber brand.
People use Uber when they want transport from one place to another and prefer an on-demand ride over driving themselves or using another transport option.
Riders want to get from pickup to destination without having to find, call or negotiate with a driver themselves.
The app can show available ride options, an estimated pickup time, route and price before or during the trip, making an on-demand ride easier to arrange.
Riders may face higher prices during busy periods, longer waits when few drivers are nearby, cancellations, service problems or safety concerns.
The rider requests a trip, confirms the pickup and destination and pays through the platform or another locally supported method.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Request / Pay — The rider tells Uber where they want to go and pays for the completed trip through the platform or another supported method. | ← Owner · Match / ETA — Uber shows the rider the matched driver, vehicle and estimated arrival information and coordinates the trip in the app. | ← Provider · Ride — The driver performs the physical transport from pickup to destination.

Explanation: A ride depends on whether Uber operates in the location, whether an eligible driver is available and whether the requested ride type can be served.
Riders usually request trips through the Uber app, with web booking available in some markets.
Riders choose a ride option, request pickup, take the trip, pay and can rate the experience afterward.
Riders bring trip demand, pickup and destination information, payment details, ratings and repeated usage that help create demand density.
Drivers are the people or licensed transport providers who make vehicles and driving time available to complete ride requests on the platform.
Drivers want access to nearby trip demand so they can turn their time and vehicle into earnings.
Uber can provide a stream of ride requests without drivers having to find each passenger themselves, while many drivers can choose when to go online.
Drivers can spend time waiting between trips and must manage costs such as fuel or charging, insurance, maintenance, rental or financing and local licensing.
Drivers receive trip offers, decide whether to accept them where permitted, pick up the rider and complete the requested ride.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Trip Offer — Uber's matching system sends a ride request to an available driver based on location and other marketplace conditions. | → Consumer · Ride — The driver performs the physical transport from pickup to destination. | ← Owner · Payout — Uber coordinates driver earnings and settlement after the trip, subject to the local pricing and fee structure. | ← Partner · Vehicle Access — Rental, leasing and fleet partners can supply eligible vehicles to drivers who need a car to participate.

Explanation: Drivers and vehicles must satisfy the legal and platform requirements that apply in the relevant market, including required documents and safety or background checks.
Drivers use the Uber Driver app to go online, receive trip requests, navigate to pickup and manage their activity and earnings.
Drivers make themselves available, accept trips, travel to pickup, transport riders and can rate riders after the trip.
Drivers contribute their time, local mobility capacity, driving skills and access to an eligible vehicle and required permits or licences.
Rental, leasing and fleet companies help drivers gain access to vehicles that meet Uber's requirements, especially when a driver does not own a suitable car.
Vehicle partners expand the pool of usable cars by renting, leasing or operating vehicles that drivers can use for ride-hailing.
They can earn rental, leasing or fleet income by serving drivers who need vehicles to participate in the Uber marketplace.
Vehicle partners have to keep cars used enough to cover their costs while managing maintenance, insurance, financing, driver quality and local regulatory requirements.
Partners provide eligible cars or fleet access to drivers under rental, leasing or employment arrangements that are usually managed outside the rider transaction itself.
Transaction Flows: → Provider · Vehicle Access — Rental, leasing and fleet partners can supply eligible vehicles to drivers who need a car to participate.

Explanation: Vehicles and fleet arrangements must meet Uber's requirements and the transport, insurance and licensing rules of the local market.
Uber connects drivers and fleet operators through vehicle-solution programs, fleet tools and local partner arrangements.
Partners acquire and maintain vehicles, manage rental or fleet arrangements and keep cars ready for eligible drivers.
They contribute vehicles, financing capacity, maintenance and fleet-management capability that can increase driver supply.
